security_spec.violation_condition: In XiangShan RTL, the Ctrl FSM entry walk loop (sPriority state at IopmpChecker.scala:1223) iterates j_indx from md_t_pre to md_t with termination condition 'j_indx =/= md_t'. After PR #204, system software can write MDCFG(m).t to any value (the old silent-clamp for t >= entry_num is removed), but the RTL walker has NO bounds check against HWCFG1.entry_num. When j_indx >= entry_num, the EntryTable SRAM (TrueDualPortSRAM at line 370-372, depth=entry_j) is accessed at an out-of-range address, returning undefined/garbage data. The FSM at lines 1234-1268 treats this garbage as valid entry_addr and entry_attribute (r/w/x), causing permission checks against random bit patterns instead of programmed rules.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: entry walk j_indx increment unbounded by hwcfg1.entry_num AND mdcfgTable SRAM read j_indx=iomdcfg.j_indx without entry_num ceiling comparison
security_spec.summary: Ctrl FSM entry walk lacks HWCFG1.entry_num bounds check; after spec removes MDCFG.t silent-clamp, out-of-bounds SRAM reads return garbage interpreted as valid entry attributes, causing privilege-level access control bypass
